about: What each building's facade is (task 017, docs/BUILDING-TYPES.md), as a session saw it in its photos: every building in the shooter's area and in view of a viewpoint (node tools/buildings.mjs lists them). By the building's name: way/<id> or relation/<id>, OpenStreetMap's, or lidar/x<x>z<z>, one the map lacks, by the middle of its outline. type, material, ground and balconies are words tools/facades.mjs lists; colour (its walls' above the ground floor), base's colour (the ground floor's, where it isn't the walls') and shutters (the roller shutters', or none) are its colour names. floors: the storeys counted in the photo, the ground floor's among them (null where they couldn't be). signs: the shop signs read in the photo, each its name and its colour. seen: the photo it was looked at in (a reference photo's id, or viewpoint:<id>); sure: false where it was small, far, blurred or half hidden. A building nobody could see in any photo is guessed by tools/world.mjs from the map and from these. not: on one the LiDAR found, what it is where a photo shows it isn't a building (task 112); tools/world.mjs leaves it out. layout (task 086, tools/layouts.mjs): on the street walls a photo shows clearly enough, where the doors and windows are, read off the wall straight on in that photo: each wall by its ends as the map has them (from, to: its left end and its right seen from outside), its photo, and its storeys from the ground floor up, each null where the photo didn't show it across the wall, else its openings left to right, each [kind, its left edge's metres from `from`, its width] (kind: window, door, garage, shop, balcony, a door or full-height window onto a balcony). unread: the street walls looked at in a photo and left, each by its ends with why.
